answer: Per-identity storage replication proofs price each fake seat in disk space. Every seat must hold a unique 2 GB basalt-style pseudorandom file derived from its own public key, and each epoch a verifier asks for 16 random crystal-sized 4 KB chunks within 3 seconds. Fetching them from a shared copy is too slow, and a nebula of 100 fakes needs 200 GB of separate disk, which grows linearly with every added seat and cannot be pooled.
